papers.title: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Unsupervised Discovery in Large Multimodal Astrophysical Datasets
papers.authors: M. Ronceray, M. Huertas-Company, A. Chanson, M. Siudek, A. Preto, M. J. Smith, J. Zoubian, C. Bonini
papers.venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Science (FM4Science)
papers.abstract: We compare AstroPT, AstroCLIP and AION representations for unsupervised discovery in matched Euclid imaging and DESI spectroscopy. A scalable density-estimation pipeline combines per-modality rarity with cross-modal misalignment to reveal model-dependent rankings, instrumental artefacts and physically coherent candidates including AGN and strong gravitational lenses.
papers.previewAlt: Euclid galaxy cutouts paired with DESI spectra for four anomaly candidates

posters.title: Variational Inference for Data-Driven Galaxy Population Priors
posters.description: A differentiable inference pipeline that jointly learns a galaxy-population prior and fast per-galaxy posteriors from catalogue photometry using DSPS and reweighted wake-sleep.
posters.previewAlt: Poster presenting the architecture and preliminary results for data-driven galaxy population priors

about.position: Incoming PhD student at CEA · Astrophysics & machine learning
bio: I am completing an MSc in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at the University of Tours. My research focuses on reusable machine-learning representations and probabilistic methods for scientific discovery in large astronomical surveys.

I have worked on multimodal anomaly detection with Euclid and DESI data, variational inference for galaxy population priors at CEA, and scientific simulation software for space instrumentation at LPP. My foundation-model benchmarking work was accepted at the ICLR 2026 FM4Science workshop.
